The test image shows a close-up of a soybean stem at a node with **gray-white cottony/fluffy fungal growth** developing at the node junction, surrounded by yellowed leaves (indicating plant decline). This is the hallmark of White Mold (Sclerotinia stem rot) — white cottony mycelium growing on the stem at nodes.

The reference images confirm: White Mold produces characteristic white, cottony mycelial masses on stems at nodes, exactly matching what's visible in the test image.
